title: Blackstone Forecasts Junk Credit Rating for Anthropic Following IPO
summary:
The AI laboratory is expected to receive a credit rating in the double-B range following its debut on the public market, meaning it will likely miss out on investment-grade status. Blackstone told investors the "high junk" outlook is a reversal of its earlier projections that the startup would secure an investment-grade rating by the end of the year, the Financial Times reports.

The rating could increase borrowing costs for Anthropic as it executes a plan to spend more than $800B on computing infrastructure through 2045. To fund its growth, the company has relied on a $63B financing deal known as Project North Star, in which Broadcom guarantees $42B in senior loans. While Anthropic reportedly holds $112B in cash, a junk rating would restrict its access to capital from insurance companies and pension funds that are barred from investing in non-investment-grade debt.

selectedTweets.text:
ANTHROPIC EXPECTED TO RECEIVE A “HIGH” JUNK CREDIT RATING AFTER IPO: FT

Blackstone has told investors Anthropic is likely to receive a credit rating in the double-B range after going public, below investment grade, reversing its earlier expectations for an investment-grade rating by year-end.

The lower rating could make it more expensive for Anthropic to finance its massive AI infrastructure expansion, while limiting access to pension funds and insurers that face restrictions on investing in junk-rated debt.

The warning comes as Blackstone participates in Anthropic's $63B financing deal, known as Project North Star, to support the leasing of 1.5 GW of Google's AI chips.

Under the deal:

• More than $42B in senior loans are guaranteed by Broadcom $AVGO.

• Another $18B in junior debt is backed by Anthropic's lease payments.

• Blackstone's funds invested $9B in junior debt, earning yields above 10%.

Anthropic's IPO prospectus outlined plans to spend more than $800B on computing infrastructure through 2045.

Without an investment-grade rating, Anthropic may need to continue relying on financially stronger partners to support its borrowing.

The major credit agencies, Moody's, S&P and Fitch, have not yet formally issued ratings for Anthropic, per FT.
